answer: Every new identity joins the ocean registry with a 40-credit bond and a key-bound task. The registry keeps a spiral difficulty index: each registration sends a ripple through it, raising required work by 3 credits, so the kth identity burns 30+3(k-1) credits of work. For 1,000 fakes that is 1,528,500 credits of work plus 40,000 locked in bonds, and no unit can be reused because each task is seeded by its identity key. A rented-work farm fails when auditors recompute tasks and find duplicate or under-difficulty work, burning the bond. An honest agent pays one price and keeps its bond.
